steps.body: Since any grouping works, choose deliberately: a ten-partner pair if one exists, otherwise a double, otherwise simply left to right.
steps.narration: Since any grouping works, choose deliberately: a ten-partner pair if one exists, otherwise a double, otherwise simply left to right.

widget.prompt: The addends include 6 and 4. Fill the frame to confirm they make ten.
widget.missFeedback: Fill one square at a time, counting as you go.
widget.successFeedback: Ten filled — 6 and 4 are the pair worth grouping first.

predict.prompt: Which pair should you look for FIRST in three addends?
predict.reveal: A ten-partner pair makes the remaining step trivial, so it is worth finding first. With 8 + 6 + 2, grabbing the two biggest gives 8 + 6 = 14, a mid-teens subtotal with no benchmark to lean on — while pairing 8 and 2 makes ten and leaves the easiest possible finish, 10 + 6.

widget.prompt: To add 8 + 2 + 6, which two should you group first?

options.label: 8 and 2
options.feedback: Correct — 8 and 2 make exactly ten, which leaves an easy ten-plus-6 to finish.

options.label: 8 and 6
options.feedback: This pair does not land on ten, so the last step stays awkward.

options.label: 2 and 6
options.feedback: This pair misses the ten that 8 and 2 would have made together.

options.label: No pair helps here
options.feedback: One pair does make ten; scanning for ten-partners first is the whole strategy.

hints: Look for two addends that make ten.
Ten plus the rest is easy to name.

options.label: Any order — all three are small
options.feedback: Correct — with three small addends no grouping is clearly faster, so any order is fine.

options.label: Only left to right is allowed
options.feedback: Addition permits any grouping; left-to-right is a habit, not a rule.

options.label: Make ten first
options.feedback: These addends are too small to reach ten as a pair, so there is no ten to make.

options.label: Use a double
options.feedback: A double is possible here, but with addends this small, any order is just as fast — no strategy saves real time.

hints: The addends can be grouped in any order.
Grouping changes the work, not the total.

widget.prompt: Which pair is the helpful double in 4 + 5 + 5?

options.label: 5 and 5
options.feedback: Correct — a known double is instant, so double first and then join the 4.

options.label: 4 and 5
options.feedback: This pair mixes the odd addend with only one of the 5s, so it is not the double; group the two 5s instead.

options.label: There is no double here
options.feedback: A double is right here — two of the addends are both 5, so 5 + 5 is the double to use.

options.label: No pair can help
options.feedback: Saving the hardest pair for last does not use the double you already know.

hints: The addends can be grouped in any order.
Grouping changes the work, not the total.
